round_scores.evidence: Agent D explains: "It's Ramadan starting tomorrow. I'll be fasting, so I can't eat until after sunset. That's around 7.10." No disagreement expressed.

Agent A proposes moving dinner to 7.15: "can we just move dinner to 7.15..." Agent B objects: "7.15 is too late for me. I start work at 6 a.m., so I need to eat much earlier." Incompatible scheduling demands appear.

Agent C suggests keeping 6.30 and D eat later: "So we cook at 6.30 as usual. Agent D, you just eat later?" Agent D rejects that as undermining the social goal: "But then I'd be eating alone. The point of the rota is we eat together, isn't it?" Positions and the stakes (social togetherness vs scheduling) become clearer.

Agents clarify different interpretations of the rota: C: "I thought the point was only having to cook once a week." D: "I guess that's part of it. But for me, it's also about getting to eat with everyone." The substantive disagreement about the rota's purpose persists.

A endorses D's social rationale: "She's right. That's the whole point, isn't it? For us to eat together." C notes the scheduling incompatibility: "Right, but Agent B can't eat at 7.15 and Agent D can't eat at 6.30. So...?" The core incompatibility remains unresolved.

D offers a compromise: "You all carry on and eat at 6.30. I'll just sit with you, and then I can eat my share after sunset." A pushes back on whether that satisfies the social goal: "But that's not really eating together, is it? You'd just be watching us." The compromise is proposed but not yet accepted by all.

B accepts the compromise: "That works for me. We're still at the table together." C also: "Works for me." With two housemates accepting D's proposal the level of conflict drops, though A's objection still stands.

D: "It's not perfect, but it's okay for me. The main thing is that we're all still at the table together." A then assents: "Okay. If you're sure, then." All parties accept the concrete arrangement: continue cooking/eating at 6.30 while D sits with them and eats after sunset.
D repeats confirmation/thanks: "Yes, I'm sure. Thanks, everyone." No substantive disagreement.

substantive_insights: Tension was between synchronizing meal time for religious observance and individual scheduling constraints (early work).
The group valued social co-presence (eating together) enough that sitting together while one person delayed eating was an acceptable trade-off.
Resolution worked because the person asking for accommodation (D) proposed a concrete concession (eat later but remain at table), which the others could accept without changing their schedules.
